subject: Hosted vs Dedicated - latency & throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-10T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated - initial follow-up and numbers recap

Hi Tom,

Thanks again for the call earlier - great context on FinPay's fraud-detection use case. Quick recap of what I heard and the open items so we can align next steps: 

Summary of requirements you shared
- Endpoint type: real-time scoring for fraud model (single-turn requests, JSON inputs)
- P95 latency target: <= 100 ms (you mentioned ideal is 60-80 ms)
- Average throughput: 120 requests/sec sustained during peak windows; burst to ~250 req/s for short windows
- Typical payload: 512 tokens request, 100-200 tokens response (depending on actions)
- Model: fine-tuned open model family (customer-managed weights) but you want Redwood to serve the inference

Initial recommendation
- Dedicated capacity is likely the best fit if p95 < 100 ms at sustained 120 req/s is mandatory, since it gives predictable tail latency and reserved GPU pools.
- Hosted API could work for an initial POC or lower-SLA paths; however, pure hosted mode may see variable tail latency under noisy-neighbor or regional congestion unless you commit to higher tiers.

Attachments: I ran a short internal micro-benchmark with similar model shape and included the results (latency-benchmarks.pdf). Those numbers are a reference, not a guarantee - we'll need to run your exact model and tokens.

Open questions for you
1) Do you need an SLA on p95 latency day-one, or is a performance acceptance window for the POC acceptable?
2) Any procurement timing or approvals we should factor in (SOW/PO terms)?
3) Would you be open to a 2-week dedicated trial (reserved capacity with a trial commit) vs a hosted pilot?

Next steps I propose
- If you want, we'll schedule a 30-min technical deep dive (solutions engineer) to validate exact model profile and run a controlled latency test with your artifact.
- Meanwhile I'll put together a recommended Dedicated config and a Hosted pilot alternative with estimated cost delta.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachment: latency-benchmarks.pdf (summary of internal micro-benchmarks)

Thanks Marissa - this is helpful. A few clarifications: 

- The p95 latency SLA is a hard requirement for production. For the POC we can accept a relaxed SLA, but we will need a plan to hit production numbers within the pilot window.
- Procurement: we typically need an SOW and PO for any reserved capacity. Budget has been provisionally approved for Q2, but final sign-off depends on pricing and SLA.
- Autoscaling: do you support fast scale-up for short bursts? During payment spikes we will see rapid traffic changes.

I've attached our SLA requirements spreadsheet so you can see the thresholds we use. Also adding Marcus (platform lead) to help with technical questions.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-11T12:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated - initial follow-up and plan options

Appreciate the quick reply and the SLA spreadsheet, Tom. Actionable follow-up and proposal: 

1) Proposed path: run a 2-week technical POC with your model artifact in our hosted environment (to validate functional behavior and baseline latency). Parallel to that, we will provision a small Dedicated pool for controlled latency testing (warm KV cache, continuous batching disabled for lowest tail latency) so we can compare head-to-head.

2) Autoscaling and bursts: our Dedicated offering supports pre-warmed burst capacity and can be configured with reactive autoscaling policies tuned for sub-100 ms p95. For hosted, burst behavior depends on capacity tier; we can enable burst credits for short windows but the tail may be less predictable than reserved Dedicated.

3) Timeline & procurement: If you approve, we can start the POC the week of Feb 16. For Dedicated trial commits we typically use a short-term trial contract or trial PO. I'll attach a short proposal doc with the recommended Dedicated sizing and the hosted pilot alternative.

4) Next step: schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with Neha to map model artifact, token profile, and exact test plan. Is Wednesday Feb 18 at 10am PT good?

I'll follow up with a one-page proposal and the proposed Dedicated config.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachment: rdw-dedicated-proposal.docx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-12T09:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated - technical deep dive items

Hi Tom - quick intro, I am the solutions engineer who will run the latency tests with you. A few technical notes ahead of the deep dive: 

- To hit a p95 <= 100 ms at 120 req/s with ~600 tokens total (request+response), we recommend Dedicated capacity with 3-4 GPU instances sized for low-latency inference. For rough sizing we expect 4x A10G-class GPUs or equivalent for your modeled load.
- Key levers to control tail latency: 1) disable aggressive batching for production scoring endpoints, 2) use KV cache warm-up and pre-loading for repeated context, 3) pin model version for deterministic kernel selection.
- For burst handling, Dedicated supports pre-warmed spare slots and configurable burst policies. We can set a policy to keep a small warm buffer which will absorb short spikes to ~250 req/s for short periods.
- Test plan: 1) baseline hosted run with your artifact and representative payloads, 2) Dedicated reserved run with identical payloads and warm caches, 3) compare p50/p95/p99 and token cost.

I'll bring a short runbook to the call showing exact perf tests and the telemetry we will capture (token latency breakdown, kernel durations, GPU utilization). Wednesday Feb 18 10am PT works for me.

Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
